abstract_sentences.text: Translating the internal representations and computations of models into concepts that humans can understand is a key goal of interpretability.

evidence.anchor: internal representations and computations of models into concepts that humans can understand

abstract_sentences.text: While recent dictionary learning methods such as Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) provide a promising route to discover human-interpretable features, they often only recover token-specific, noisy, or highly local concepts.

evidence.anchor: token-specific, noisy, or highly local concepts

abstract_sentences.text: We argue that this limitation stems from neglecting the temporal structure of language, where semantic content typically evolves smoothly over sequences.

evidence.anchor: neglecting the temporal structure of language

abstract_sentences.text: Building on this insight, we introduce Temporal Sparse Autoencoders (T-SAEs), which incorporate a novel contrastive loss encouraging consistent activations of high-level features over adjacent tokens.

evidence.anchor: contrastive loss encouraging consistent activations of high-level features over adjacent tokens

abstract_sentences.text: This simple yet powerful modification enables SAEs to disentangle semantic from syntactic features in a self-supervised manner.

evidence.anchor: disentangle semantic from syntactic features in a self-supervised manner

abstract_sentences.text: Across multiple datasets and models, T-SAEs recover smoother, more coherent semantic concepts without sacrificing reconstruction quality.

evidence.anchor: smoother, more coherent semantic concepts without sacrificing reconstruction quality

abstract_sentences.text: Strikingly, they exhibit clear semantic structure despite being trained without explicit semantic signal, offering a new pathway for unsupervised interpretability in language models.

evidence.anchor: clear semantic structure despite being trained without explicit semantic signal

final_judgment.single_storyline: Language semantics/context are expected to persist across nearby tokens while syntax is local; a contrastive loss on a designated high-level SAE split makes the residual low-level split absorb local variation, improving semantic/context readability while retaining reconstruction and steering utility.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the two latent-variable assumptions, SAE/Matryoshka reconstruction, bidirectional temporal contrastive loss, 20:80 split, MMLU probes, Table 1 standard metrics, long-sequence Figures 1/4, HH-RLHF and steering Figure 5, and Table 2 mechanism ablations.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A-D move the linearized loss, detailed HH-RLHF rankings/examples, steering prompts/strengths/features/failures, split smoothness and absorption, 8B scaling, cross-dataset probes, expanded t-SNE plots, and baseline “the” feature IDs.
final_judgment.best_pattern: A shared spliced-sequence figure establishes the temporal intuition, formal latent assumptions and loss follow, t-SNE is paired with sparse probing, Table 1 puts semantic gains beside reconstruction costs, and difference-form ablations identify the split/pair/loss tradeoff.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Semantic disentanglement is supported by proxy labels, t-SNE, smoothness, LLM feature explanations, and limited cases rather than ground-truth semantic factors or causal intervention. “Significant” and “without significant cost” lack complete uncertainty reporting, and steering is judge/description dependent.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: When adding a structural prior to a representation learner, fix the intended feature granularity and test it with task probes, standard reconstruction, long-sequence visualization, and deletion/substitution ablations so gains, costs, and mechanism are jointly visible.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule fits ordered inputs whose target concepts persist over an adjacent or explicitly defined window. Rapid semantic shifts, absent temporal order, or concepts requiring other time scales can make smoothness erase signal; multi-scale or different priors are then needed. This paper's memory/compute, geometry, single-layer/two-model, and short-scaling limits constrain extrapolation.

statistical_analysis.aggregation_units: MMLU token/question activations for probes; active features over sequences for Smoothness; one activation mean per HH-RLHF completion; 30 steering features for judge scores.
statistical_analysis.central_quantities: probe accuracy, FVE, Cosine Similarity, Fraction Alive, Smoothness, Autointerp score, rejected-minus-chosen activation difference, token-length difference, Pearson correlation, intervention success, coherence.
statistical_analysis.dispersion_or_intervals: Autointerp, absorption, and Table 10 values report standard deviations; most results have no uncertainty display.
statistical_analysis.hypothesis_tests: Two-sided t-test for rejected/chosen response length gives p=9e−10; Figure 6 annotates several Pearson-correlation p-values.
statistical_analysis.seed_task_dataset_levels: Seeds are not reported; task/dataset levels are explicit for MMLU, Wikipedia, FineFineWeb, The Pile, and HH-RLHF first 1,000 samples.
statistical_analysis.decision_quantities: relative probe accuracy, mean metric differences in Table 2, Pareto tradeoff in Figure 5, and top-15 feature rankings in Table 6.
